questions.question: Why did the study use separate reference levels of theory for periodic and non-periodic systems?

options.A: Hybrid wB97X-D3BJ was selected for non-periodic systems, while PBE-D3 was used periodically because hybrid periodic calculations were too costly
options.B: PBE-D3 was used only for clusters, while hybrid DFT was required for all periodic cells
options.C: The authors avoided all DFT and relied solely on classical force fields
options.D: Hybrid functionals were chosen for metals because they scale linearly in periodic systems

questions.rationale: The paper pairs high-quality cluster labels with tractable periodic PBE labels, noting the expense of periodic hybrid calculations.
questions.evidence_quote: we selected wB97X-D3BJ/def2-TZVPD as our reference level of theory for non-periodic systems and PBE-D3 in a plane wave basis as our reference level of theory for periodic systems. We also labeled a random subset of non-periodic systems with PBE-D3 to improve the information exchange between output heads in our multitask learning scheme. Unfortunately, the great expense of hybrid functionals such as wB97X-D3BJ for periodic systems means that it was not feasible to label our periodic dataset with this level of theory.

questions.question: Why did the authors prefer GFN1-xTB partial charges over GFN2-xTB or GFN0-xTB?

options.A: GFN1-xTB gave the best compromise between charge accuracy and convergence across isolated and periodic systems
options.B: GFN1-xTB was the only method that could label periodic energies
options.C: GFN2-xTB charges failed only for organic molecules, while GFN0-xTB was exact
options.D: GFN1-xTB was selected because it required no charge labels

questions.rationale: The charge model was selected empirically for balanced accuracy and convergence across the mixed system types.
questions.evidence_quote: Instead, we tested reference atomic partial charges from GFN1-xTB, GFN2-xTB, and GFN0-xTB [16] [17] [18] , and found the older GFN1-xTB to be the most suitable for generating charge labels for SEI training sets, because it achieves the best compromise between accuracy and convergence across isolated and periodic systems

questions.question: What did adding the SPICE organic-chemistry data do to validation error, and what did the authors infer?

options.A: PBE-head RMSE did not increase and hybrid-head RMSE rose only 8%, suggesting unused latent-space capacity
options.B: Both heads' RMSE doubled, showing the model could not share information
options.C: PBE-head RMSE rose 8% and hybrid-head RMSE fell to zero
options.D: SPICE improved only periodic predictions because it contained no battery chemistry

questions.rationale: The modest error effect despite wider chemical scope suggests multitask latent capacity could be used to broaden applicability.
questions.evidence_quote: We observed no increase in PBE-head validation RMSE on the battery datasets when adding the SPICE data, and only an 8% increase in hybrid-head RMSE, implying that the greatly increased scope of the data did not impose a heavy cost on model capacity

questions.question: How did the training batches preserve emphasis on the most relevant surface-reaction subset?

options.A: Each batch drew half its samples from the higher-priority periodic/cluster surface-reaction data and half from the rest
options.B: Each batch contained only surface-reaction data, excluding all other training examples
options.C: The surface-reaction subset was used only for validation
options.D: The model oversampled SPICE fourfold and discarded periodic examples

questions.rationale: The authors use a rehearsal-style balanced sampling scheme after doubling hidden-layer widths.
questions.evidence_quote: We used a higher-priority dataset composed only of the periodic and cluster surface reaction subset of our dataset, such that each batch was sampled half from this priority data and half from the rest of the dataset (as in rehearsal [24] ).

questions.question: What composition and scale characterized each initial SEI Simulator cell?

options.A: 700 EC molecules with 52 Li+ and 52 PF6− ions, totaling 7,416 atoms at 1 M
options.B: 700 LiPF6 pairs and 52 EC molecules, totaling 741 atoms at 0.1 M
options.C: 700 EC molecules and 33 added Li atoms, totaling 2,000 atoms
options.D: 52 EC molecules with 700 ions of each type, totaling 7,416 atoms

questions.rationale: The initial electrolyte setup and atom count are explicitly provided for the simulation cells.
questions.evidence_quote: Each system starts with 700 molecules of EC and 52 ions each of Li+ and PF 6 -, giving a 1 M solution with 7416 total atoms (Fig 1 ).

questions.question: Which added-lithium levels defined the four candidate groups, and how were they generated?

options.A: 5, 12, 23, and 33 Li+ per box, arising after 40 iterations of MD and reaction templates
options.B: 1, 2, 3, and 4 Li+ per box, manually inserted before packing
options.C: 52, 104, 156, and 208 Li+ per box, matching the salt stoichiometry
options.D: 5, 12, 23, and 33 electrons per box, added without charge compensation

questions.rationale: These are the lithiated candidate cohorts produced by the SEI Simulator after repeated MD and reaction-template steps.
questions.evidence_quote: We defined four sets of candidates with different levels of added Li: 5, 12, 23, and 33 added Li+ ions per box (levels which arose from the SEI Simulator after 40 iterations of MD and reaction templates).

questions.question: What two-stage MD protocol was used to prepare and rank each candidate structure?

options.A: Anneal at 400 K and 1,000 atm for 100 ps, then rank by mean energy over 20 ps at 300 K and 1 atm
options.B: Anneal at 300 K and 1 atm for 20 ps, then rank at 400 K and 1,000 atm for 100 ps
options.C: Run 1 ns at 400 K and rank a single instantaneous energy at 0 K
options.D: Optimize with DFT at 1,000 K, then sample at 1 atm for 1 ps

questions.rationale: The harsh NPT annealing was followed by ambient-condition trajectories for comparable energy ranking.
questions.evidence_quote: Having produced a series of unique initial geometries, we then annealed them using our reactive QRNN model with NPT MD at 400 K and 1000 atm for 100 ps each. Remarkably, our QRNN models gave stable dynamics despite the extreme conditions applied, which is often not the case for MLFFs [28] . Finally we ranked each set of candidates by calculating the mean potential energy of each structure over an MD trajectory of 20 ps length at ambient conditions of 300 K and 1 atm.

questions.question: What bond-count associations did the authors find in the most lithiated subgroup?

options.A: P–F and Li–O bonds tracked more stable structures, whereas C–O and Li–F tracked less stable ones
options.B: C–O and Li–F bonds tracked more stable structures, whereas P–F and Li–O tracked less stable ones
options.C: All four bond types were equally associated with total energy
options.D: Only Li–Li bonds were included in the stability analysis

questions.rationale: Bond counts were compared with total system energies after Lewis-structure recalculation for the 33-added-Li group.
questions.evidence_quote: We performed statistical analysis of the bonding in SEI candidate structures by recalculating the Lewis structure of the entire system based on the atomic positions after reactive MD using Schrodinger Materials Science Suite [29] , then tabulating the counts of various bond types versus the total system energy (Fig 4 ). P-F and Li-O bonds are associated with more stable structures, while C-O and Li-F bonds are associated with less stable ones.

questions.question: Why could the authors not directly validate predicted SEI density, diffusivity, viscosity, or modulus?

options.A: Experimental values for any SEI composition were unavailable, so validation instead used calculated surface reaction barriers
options.B: Their model produced no stable dynamics for any system
options.C: Those quantities were excluded because the SEI has no organic components
options.D: The available experiments contradicted the simulated values but were not reported

questions.rationale: The authors identify the absence of experimental SEI material properties as a validation obstacle and compare to best-available reaction barrier calculations instead.
questions.evidence_quote: For example, we cannot compare the density, diffusivity, viscosity, or elastic modulus of our SEI material against experimental values because such experiments do not exist for any SEI composition. Instead, we validated our model against the best available calculations for surface reaction energy barriers

questions.question: What scope limitation most directly constrains conclusions about how electrolyte formulation controls SEI structure?

options.A: Candidates were built only for 1 M LiPF6 in EC, so comparing multiple formulations remains future work
options.B: The work compared five electrolyte formulations but only one charge state
options.C: The training set excluded LiPF6 and EC entirely
options.D: All predicted candidates were experimentally synthesized and tested

questions.rationale: The authors caution that formulation comparison is needed before structure/property trends can be optimized across chemistries.
questions.evidence_quote: We have so far constructed SEI candidates using only a single formulation of electrolyte, 1M LiPF 6 in EC. Based on this common formulation, we are able to suggest plausible structures for the SEI and analyze what makes a structure more or less energetically stable. However, the full power of this technique will come from comparing multiple formulations.
